claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified now on a constrained basis because current aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal is clean, provided the certification packet reflects current results and expressly discloses the current medical-device-support limitation rather than relying on stale prior approval or informal monitoring.
decision_criteria: Claim audited: whether recommending certification is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite a current subgroup regression.

Supporting evidence: aggregate readiness passes and rehearsal shows no severity-one incidents; the subgroup regression is real; policy requires disclosure or approved mitigation; public guidance supports documenting limitations and ongoing monitoring; prior approval and informal monitoring are contextual only.
Missing evidence: the current release documentation itself, any approved mitigation or risk acceptance, and any proof that the required disclosure has been incorporated before launch.

Could the same conclusion be reached from admissible evidence alone: admissible evidence supports only a conditional conclusion that certification may proceed if current documentation is updated to disclose the limitation or approved mitigation exists; it does not support an unconditional compliant certification today.

What would change the verdict: production of the current packet/model card with the required disclosure, or an approved pre-launch risk acceptance/mitigation covering the regression, would likely move the verdict toward compliant or compliant_with_caveats.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model-card text showing the medical-device-support limitation is expressly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide any approved pre-launch risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the subgroup regression.
Provide the materiality/use-case mapping showing how the medical-device-support slice is treated in the launch packet and certification decision.
specific_concerns: The admissible record supports a conditional path to certification only if current release documentation actually discloses the material medical-device-support weakness or an approved mitigation exists before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the current model card or certification packet already contains the required disclosure language.
No approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation is attached; the only operational response in evidence is an informal post-launch monitoring comment.
The actor's packet summary overreaches if read as support for immediate certification rather than certification contingent on updated documentation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record, rather than only potentially compliant after the current documentation is updated.
That informal monitoring plus prior family approval materially strengthens compliance beyond contextual background.
That the required disclosure predicate has already been satisfied in launch materials.
